title: Heart attack victim shouldn't have been arrested: Inquest
article: Nothing could have been done to prevent Brian McPherson from dying on Aug. 27, 2011. But an inquest report reveals he shouldn't have been in a Garden Hill jail cell when he did.
McPherson was found dead of sudden heart failure in his jail cell at the police station in Garden Hill that day. A 44-page inquest report released Friday by Judge Malcolm
McDonald said there was little doubt McPherson would have died that day, regardless of whether he was in jail.

"There is, though, clear evidence that he was not lawfully arrested and that he should not have been detained and certainly not detained in cells that were overcrowded and in an unacceptable condition," McDonald wrote. "It is forseeable that others unlawfully detained and kept in such conditions could die as well if action is not taken."

McDonald said band police were called to McPherson's home to see if alcohol was being consumed, with the judge saying the call likely came from band Coun. Wayne Harper. Police and Harper eventually entered McPherson's home without permission, and Harper instructed the band constable and her volunteer assistants to arrest and detain everyone at the party.

"No one at the part y appeared to be causing trouble or to be so drunk as to not be able to care for themselves," the judge wrote. "They were not told the reasons why they were being arrested nor were they told they could speak to a lawyer."
The jail cells at Garden Hill were also in horrid condition, McDonald wrote, noting seven other people were lodged inside a cramped cell space with McPherson.

The judge made 12 recommendations. They include ensuring First Nation safety officers or band peace officers receive proper training, be properly paid and equipped and have job security, and be instructed from and supervised by professional police officers.

Minimum standards should also be established for the construction and maintenance of First Nation detention facilities, and inspected regularly to ensure a proper standard of safety and hygiene are being met.
